# Taprun

> Browser automation that doesn't burn tokens every run. AI forges a `.tap.json` program once at authoring time — the program replays deterministically forever, zero LLM at runtime. `tap doctor` catches structural drift before production breaks.

Taprun is the tool layer, not an AI layer. Any MCP host (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Cline, Continue, VS Code) connects and gets forge + run + doctor. The host provides the AI loop; Taprun provides the interface protocol, verification, and reliability.

## Vocabulary

- **tap** — the protocol, the handle, the program (`.tap.json`), and the product. One word, one concept.
- **forge** — create a tap from an observed interface (AI participates once).
- **runtime** — a platform implementation of tap's 8 core operations. Three today: Chrome Extension, Playwright (default, zero-setup), macOS (AX API + JXA + CGEvent).
- **interface** — the automation target (a website, a native app). External, not part of tap.

## 4-Layer Trust Stack

Taps bind to the highest-stability structural address available:

1. **Layer 1 — Explicit declarations (~100% deterministic):** agents.json, OpenAPI, llms.txt, JSON-LD, RSS, Open Graph. SEO/legal/subscriber incentives keep these honest. Compiled to `.tap.json` with zero AI.
2. **Layer 2 — Data contracts (~95%):** API endpoints, SSR hydration globals, WebSocket payloads. The site's own frontend depends on them.
3. **Layer 3 — Semantic structure (~80%):** ARIA roles, heading levels, data-testid, itemprop, Schema.org. W3C-standardized, captured via fingerprint.
4. **Layer 4 — Implementation details (~30%):** CSS classes, framework attrs (data-v-*, _ngcontent), DOM nesting. No external stability driver. Never hashed.

Doctor cross-validates across layers. If Layer 1 JSON-LD says `Product.name = "iPhone 16 Pro"` but the tap's DOM extraction returns `title = "iPhone Case"`, the tap navigated to the wrong structural location — "valid type, wrong node."

## Install

```
npx -y @taprun/cli --version          # zero-install (any Node host)
curl -fsSL https://taprun.dev/install.sh | sh   # permanent binary (macOS/Linux)
```

## Connect to any MCP host

```
tap mcp connect
```

Or add manually to your MCP config:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "tap": { "command": "tap", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

## First commands

```
tap github/trending              # run a community tap (slash form, not space)
tap hackernews/hot
tap forge https://news.ycombinator.com    # Tier 0 — compile without AI (API/JSON-LD/RSS)
tap forge "get Hacker News top stories"   # BYOK AI path (Claude / OpenAI / Ollama)
tap doctor                       # check fleet health
tap watch github/trending --every 5m      # follow changes over time
```

## Pricing

- **Free** — 140+ community taps, full doctor, Tier 0 forge, watch, MCP read ops. 3-day trial on paid features.
- **Hacker ($9/mo)** — full forge pipeline through any MCP host. BYOK AI key.
- **Pro ($29/mo)** — auto-heal, auto-refresh, scheduled runs, team MCP server. 100% local.

## Security invariants

- Taprun servers never push executable code to clients.
- Taprun servers never initiate connections to user machines.
- Tap source never leaves the user's machine (multi-machine sync, when built, is end-to-end encrypted client-side).
- Server features are opt-in, off by default.
- Local-first is the architectural default, not a fallback.
